modelAnswer:
We sat down next to each other, but David wouldn't look at me. He kept staring at his shoes. "The kids from other schools might laugh at me," he whispered at last. I didn't argue. Instead, I reminded him of every practice he had never missed and every run he had finished, however long it took. "You don't run to beat anyone, David. You run to finish, and you always do." He was silent for a long moment. Then he lifted his head. "I want to run," he said quietly but firmly.

I watched as David moved up to the starting line with the other runners. When the signal sounded, the crowd rushed into the forest and soon left him far behind. I waited near the finish line. One by one, the runners came out of the trees, until only David was missing. At last, a small figure appeared at the edge of the forest, his body rocking from side to side. His teammates, who had finished long before, ran back and called out his name. Children from other schools joined in. Nobody laughed. David pushed on and crossed the finish line. When he turned to me, his big toothy smile was back. He had not won, but once again, he had finished.

paragraphs.ending: He had not won, but once again, he had finished. 结尾落在“跑完”而非“获胜”，与原文的“总能跑完”首尾呼应，不额外喊口号。

alternatives: 也可让教练或本校同学过来一起劝David，只要第一段结束时他已决定参赛。
